Hi all — I reviewed the draft copy and the attached assets. Below are my recommended edits and a short set of hero variants to test in the marketplace listing. I've attached an editable doc (aws_listing_copy_v2.docx) with tracked changes.

Key copy notes (short):
- Lead with clear buyer value: "Reduce inference cost for multimodal applications" is stronger than a feature-first headline.
- Avoid deep technical taxonomy in the hero; move architecture details to the technical description.
- Call out deployment options (Hosted API, Dedicated, AMI) in the product features section with entitlement notes.
- Pricing footnote: if trial tokens are free, note the duration and whether they count toward AWS billing entitlements.

Hero headline variants (prioritized):
1) "High-performance LLM inference at production scale" — clear, enterprise-friendly.
2) "Fast, predictable LLM serving with cost controls" — focuses on economics.
3) "Deploy inference where you run — hosted, dedicated, or AMI" — emphasizes flexibility.

Suggested subhead (single): "Unified runtime for predictable latency, lower per-token cost, and simple rollout across cloud and on-prem."

Suggested bullets for product page (short):
- Low-latency, GPU-optimized inference (auto-batching & caching)
- Dedicated pools and private VPC options for compliance-sensitive workloads
- Cost controls: intelligent batching, quantization recommendations, and token-level telemetry
- Co-sell readiness: AWS badging + partner contact included in listing

Attachments in my email: aws_listing_copy_v2.docx (editable copy), pricing_table_q2.csv (please confirm footnote).

Aditya — can you confirm the entitlement language we should publish for AMI (i.e., whether AMI-based deployments are eligible for the same trial / private-offer flows)?
